sections.html:
Arlington is a small, fully urban county directly across the Potomac River from Washington, D.C. It covers about 26 square miles and had 238,643 residents in the 2020 census. Fairfax County, the City of Falls Church and the City of Alexandria are its neighbors, and there are no separate towns inside the county lines.

Four Metro lines (Orange, Blue, Silver and Yellow) and Interstates 395 and 66 serve the county. Buyers here often shop by neighborhood, with Rosslyn, Clarendon, Ballston, Pentagon City and Court House the names that come up most. Every parcel is assessed as of January 1 each year, so the number on your notice is where any question about your tax bill begins.

Arlington bills real estate tax in two equal installments. The first is due June 15 and the second is due October 5. If a date lands on a weekend or holiday, a payment made the next business day avoids the late penalty. Owners are expected to know the due dates under the Code of Virginia, so a bill that never arrived is not an excuse for paying late.

  • If your mortgage company pays through escrow, you get no bill unless the Treasurer's Office does not receive the escrow payment.
  • If you sold and the buyer is now responsible, send the bill back to the Treasurer's Office with whatever you know about the new owner.
  • Send billing address changes in writing to the Department of Real Estate Assessments.

State law caps what a locality can charge on a late bill. The penalty cannot top 10 percent of the tax past due or $10, whichever is greater, and interest cannot top 10 percent a year.

sections.h2: What is the Arlington real estate tax rate?
sections.html: For calendar year 2025 the rate was $1.033 per $100 of assessed value. Commercial property, such as office buildings and hotels, pays an extra $0.125 per $100. The County Board sets the rate each April, so a later year may differ. Read the figure on your current bill before you plan around any number you see online.

Assessments take effect as of January 1 and are mailed and posted online each January. The county defines fair market value as the price a property would bring under normal conditions.

To get there, the county studies a 12-month window of sales that starts 16 months before the effective date. For 2026 that window ran from September 1, 2024 through August 31, 2025. Because the county looks at every sale in a neighborhood, one unusual sale has only a small pull on your value. If a sale of your own house is recent, it still counts as one data point among many.

There are four steps, and you can skip some of them. Each has its own deadline.

Appeal stepWhere to goTiming
Informal talkNeighborhood appraiser, 703-228-3920 or assessments@arlingtonva.usBefore you file anything
Department Review RequestDepartment of Real Estate AssessmentsEarly March: use the date printed on your notice
Board of EqualizationSeven county residents appointed each yearApril 15
Circuit Court1425 North Courthouse Road, 703-228-7010Final option

If you have no determination letter by April 1, file the Board of Equalization appeal anyway to keep that door open. You may go straight to the board without a department review. The board works independently of the assessment office.

sections.h2: What happens in a department review?
sections.html:
An appraiser contacts you to schedule an inspection, usually inside and outside the house with a second appraiser present. The appraiser writes a recommendation, a supervisor reviews it, and the Director of Real Estate Assessments makes the final call. You get written notice by mail or email. A review can lower the value, confirm it or raise it, so go in with comparable sales rather than a hunch.

You can withdraw or refuse the inspection, though the review then runs on the information the county already has. If someone files for you, the county requires a signed letter of authorization from the owner.

sections.h2: Tax relief for older and disabled owners
sections.html:
The Real Estate Tax Relief Program offers an exemption or a deferral to homeowners 65 and older and to those who are totally and permanently disabled. The filing deadline is November 15. Call the county to confirm the date for the current cycle.

The county listed 2025 limits of annual income up to $105,937 and assets, not counting the home, up to $499,709 for an exemption or $674,606 for a deferral. A separate exemption covers an owner with a 100 percent service-connected, permanent and total disability, and a surviving spouse may qualify. The limits change over time, so confirm them before you file.

Settle the question of who pays at closing. The Treasurer's Office says responsibility for the tax should be worked out in the sale settlement, and your settlement attorney can tell you how it will be handled.

Under Virginia Code section 58.1-3340, the tax is a lien on the real estate that ranks ahead of other liens until it is paid, and the seller's share for the year is prorated by contract. On the deed, section 58.1-802 sets a grantor tax of 50 cents per $500, usually paid by the seller, and section 58.1-801 sets the state recordation tax at 25 cents per $100.

Before the closing date, ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure and keep the receipt for the title company.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense in Arlington?
sections.html:
A cash sale can help when a house needs work you do not want to pay for, when taxes or a loan have fallen behind, or when you are leaving the area on a short timeline. With two installments a year, an unpaid June or October bill can grow fast on a house that sits empty.

Compare any offer, ours included, with the county's January 1 value on your notice. We buy as is and give a written cash offer. Call or text with the address and we will take it from there.

faqs.q: When are Arlington County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: June 15 and October 5. If a date falls on a weekend or holiday, paying the next business day avoids the penalty.

faqs.q: What was Arlington's real estate tax rate for 2025?
faqs.a: $1.033 per $100 of assessed value, plus $0.125 per $100 for commercial property. The County Board sets the rate each April.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal an Arlington assessment to the Board of Equalization?
faqs.a: April 15. Forms must be delivered, postmarked or filed online by midnight that day.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Arlington assessment?
faqs.a: The Department of Real Estate Assessments at 703-228-3920, at 2100 Clarendon Blvd, Suite 502, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Meetings are by appointment.

faqs.q: Can I get tax relief in Arlington if I am over 65?
faqs.a: Possibly. The Real Estate Tax Relief Program covers owners 65 and older and those totally and permanently disabled, subject to income and asset limits. The filing deadline is November 15.
